newsitem.title: USA: Wolverine World Wide orders up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wolverine World Wide orders up 22 pct.

text.p: Wolverine World Wide Inc., which makes and markets branded footwear including Hush Puppies shoes and Wolverine outdoor footwear, said incoming orders for its core businesses are running 22 percent above last year.

The shoe manufacturer reported earnings for its fiscal second quarter ended June 14, 1997, rose 36 percent from the same period a year ago to $7.4 million. Earnings per share increased 31 percent to $0.17. Sales were up 36 percent to $127.8 million.
In the first six months of fiscal 1997, Wolverine World Wide's earnings rose 37 percent to $12.1 million and earnings per share grew 33 percent to $0.28. Sales increased 44 percent to $257.1 million.

"Sales in our core businesses outpaced the first six months of 1996 by nearly 24 percent, while the recently acquired Hy-Test Boots and Shoes and Hush Puppies U.K. businesses are operating at planned sales levels," said Geoffrey Bloom, Wolverine World Wide chairman and chief executive officer.
Bloom said the company's Caterpillar Footwear Group, launched early in 1997, doubled domestic sales and grew international sales by 57 percent during the first half of its fiscal year.
Hush Puppies' 57 retail stores in the U.S. reported an eight percent same store sales increase despite a slowdown in the retail sector in recent months, it said.
Shares of Wolverine World Wide were trading off 1-5/8 to 27-1/2.
